![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14096165/assets/f54c771d1b7045bbaa301c9d595a45dc64fbdfc6b1c83c152fb6fc892373ea06.png)

Describe the shaded region shown above using set-builder notation.

$$
{(x,y)\in {{field-1}}\,:\,y\,{{field-2}}\,-1}
$$
worked_solution:
Since all points $P(x,y)$ in our set lie at integer values of $x$ and $y,$ we have $x\in Z,y\in Z,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in Z\times Z={Z}^{2}.
$$

The points in our set include all those that lie *above* the line $y=-1.$ For those points, the following condition is satisfied:

$$
y>-1
$$

Also, notice that some points in our set lie *on* the line. We include these points by changing the inequality symbol above as follows:

$$
y\ge -1
$$

Therefore, we can write the set as follows:

$$
{(x,y)\in {Z}^{2}\,:\,y\ge -1}
$$
